subject.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture

question: Should OpenClaw expose all five memory role selectors now as a routing and activation foundation with per-agent inheritance, or narrow the public contract to roles that already have dedicated generic lifecycle APIs?
rationale: The permanence, lifecycle meaning, inheritance behavior, and compatibility lifetime of public persisted plugin role selectors cannot be safely authorized from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Narrow to complete roles
options.body: Expose only roles with complete generic runtime contracts now, migrate legacy config through doctor, and defer the remaining selectors.

options.title: Approve routing foundation
options.body: Ship all five selectors as ownership and activation contracts, explicitly documenting which behavior remains plugin-owned or deferred.

options.title: Pause for RFC
options.body: Hold the implementation until the linked RFC settles taxonomy, inheritance, lifecycle, and compatibility semantics.

recommendation.title: Narrow to complete roles
recommendation.body: Expose only roles with complete generic runtime contracts now, migrate legacy config through doctor, and defer the remaining selectors.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the central slot, loader, and plugin configuration surfaces affected by this public contract.
